tweet_summary: Rep. Thomas Massie tells incoming Acting AG Blanche he has 30 days to release Epstein files or be criminally liable under the Epstein Files Transparency Act (H.R. 4405).
why_note_decision: H.R. 4405 (Public Law 119-38, signed Nov 19, 2025) DOES require the Attorney General to make Epstein records public within 30 days of enactment. The original note correctly states the bill's 30-day records release but claims 'the Act contains no provisions for criminal liability' — this is technically a real point (the bill's enforcement mechanism is contempt/judicial review, not specific criminal penalties on the AG), but Massie's framing is standard political-pressure rhetoric on a real legal obligation. Raters dominantly tagged it note-not-needed (16) and missing-key-points (14) — they did not view the criminal-liability framing as misleading enough to warrant correction. The post is high-volume but the original note is a partisan pedantry intervention; raters did not consider it helpful.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. Massie's tweet correctly references H.R. 4405's 30-day release deadline (Public Law 119-38, signed Nov 19, 2025). The 'criminally liable' framing is political rhetoric on a real legal obligation; the underlying 30-day deadline is accurate. Any note technically litigating whether the bill has explicit criminal-liability language without context is a false positive that raters rejected.

original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Partisan pedantry — confirms the substantive 30-day deadline Massie cited, then nitpicks the 'criminally liable' rhetoric without genuine misinformation impact.

fact_check.claim_verdict: Tweet's 30-day claim is accurate per H.R. 4405. 'Criminally liable' is political rhetoric on a real legal obligation.
fact_check.notes: Bill was signed Nov 19, 2025; 30-day deadline ~Dec 19, 2025. Massie tweet from April 2026 is in context of acting AG transition.
